# Test fixtures

| File | Source | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| `mona_lisa_330.jpg` | Leonardo da Vinci, *Mona Lisa* (c. 1503–1519), Wikimedia Commons file `Mona_Lisa,_by_Leonardo_da_Vinci,_from_C2RMF_retouched.jpg`, 330 px thumbnail (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mona_Lisa,_by_Leonardo_da_Vinci,_from_C2RMF_retouched.jpg) | Public domain (PD-Art: faithful reproduction of a 2D work whose author died more than 100 years ago) |

Why a painting: face-detector tests need a face, and the rule is no photos of real living people.
A 500-year-old public-domain painting gives a real-looking face with an unambiguous licence.
Codes (segno, python-barcode) and plates (rendered text) are generated in the tests.
